title: What is React
description: Understand what React is, its history, and why it's the most popular frontend library.

data.text: **React** is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. It was created by Jordan Walke, a software engineer at Facebook, and was first deployed on Facebook's newsfeed in 2011. React was open-sourced in 2013 and has since become one of the most popular frontend libraries in the world.

React solves the problem of building large applications with data that changes over time. Before React, developers had to manually update the DOM (Document Object Model) whenever data changed, which was error-prone and inefficient.

items: **Declarative**: React makes it painless to create interactive UIs. Design simple views for each state in your application, and React will efficiently update and render just the right components when your data changes.
**Component-Based**: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.
**Learn Once, Write Anywhere**: You can develop new features in React without rewriting existing code. React can also render on the server using Node and build mobile apps using React Native.

data.text: Before diving into code, let's understand the core concepts that make React powerful:

items: **Components**: The building blocks of React applications. They are reusable pieces of UI.
**JSX**: A syntax extension that allows you to write HTML-like code in JavaScript.
**State**: Data that changes over time in your application.
**Props**: Short for properties, how you pass data from parent to child components.
**Virtual DOM**: A lightweight copy of the actual DOM that React uses for efficient updates.

data.title: React is a Library, Not a Framework
data.text: Unlike Angular or Vue, React is a library focused solely on the view layer. It doesn't include built-in solutions for routing, state management, or HTTP requests. This gives you the freedom to choose the best tools for your project.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces
React uses a Virtual DOM for efficient updates
It's declarative, making code more predictable and easier to debug
data.takeaway: Next, we'll set up your development environment to start building React applications.
